PoiDestination draws one of the nine client GasWeightArea volumes by weight, draws a point inside it, and walks every phase centre along the straight line to it. rows.source: docs/118 s3 - Cranberry's own weighting rule over the client's own footprints
rows.note: weight = (client footprint area) ^ exponent. 0.5 weights by the box's own linear extent rather than its area, so SchadeWoodsLoggingTrail (137,900 m2) is drawn 4.5x as often as ChangsWildCampgrounds (6,802 m2) instead of 20x; 1.0 weights strictly by area and 0 makes the nine equally likely. The AREAS are the client's [CLIENT]; that a bigger volume is a likelier destination is this project's reading of what a weight volume is for, and the exponent is how hard that reading is applied. 0.5 rather than 1.0 because at 1.0 one volume takes 40 % of every match, and the drop lane's own signed-off property - three consecutive matches are never the same place - fails at exactly one window in 200 (DropPlannerTests.ConsecutiveMatchesDropSomewhereElse); at 0.5 it holds with the client's volumes still driving the draw (docs/118 s3.4).

Arms and drives resource 611 while a match runs, so the meter the client already draws (HudPlayerResourcesWindow.gfx ResourceType.TOXICITY / m_toxicity) stops rendering empty for every second of every match. CRANBERRY_GAS_TOXICITY=0 turns it off; nothing else in the gas path reads it, so off is byte-identical to the pre-D279 wire. September 6: this is now a HUD-send switch only. Authoritative toxicity and damage continue regardless of its value.
The client's own row: Generic^611^75^ResourceToxicity^14118^14119^... Not a ruling - it is the id the client's own Resources.PlayerResourceDataSource keys the meter on.

Unlike health (1/1) and stamina (6/6) the toxicity row's type is NOT its id: 611 is the id, 75 is the type. The 8d ResourceEvent carries both, so getting them the wrong way round is a silent no-op on the client's lookup.

The full meter, and the number that CONTRADICTS Z1's ToxicityMax = 100 (ZoneGasRetail.cs:348). The client wins: it is the client's own bar and the client's own percentage calc. INITIAL_VALUE on the same row is 0 and there are no VALUE_MARKER tiers, so the meter is a plain 0 -> 180,000 fill.

1 per millisecond charged on a REGEN_TICK_MSEC = 1000 beat is 1,000 units a second, i.e. 180 s from empty to full - the client's own fill rate, and what the owner's ruling (d) names. FLAG_INIT_WITH_DISABLED_REGEN = 1 on the same row is why it does not run until the server arms it.
The beat REGEN_PER_MS is charged on. Equal to GasSettings.TickPeriodMs, which is why the server's own accumulator moves in whole ticks and stays in step with a client that ticks the resource itself.

rows.source: docs/118 s4 - Cranberry's own symmetric drain; the client's own BURN_PER_MSEC on Resources.txt:145 is 0
rows.note: The one toxicity number the client does NOT supply. Its BURN_PER_MSEC is 0 and FLAG_INIT_WITH_DISABLED_BURN is 1, so a client-side drain from the row's own columns would drain nothing at all - the drain has to be a server number or there is no drain. 1,000 units a second mirrors the client's own fill exactly (180 s out, 180 s back), which is the only choice that needs no second story about why the two differ.

The ENUM MEMBER NAME. ce 01's +0x54 is the time constant of the client's own exponential ease (docs/18 s1, G-07), so a wall re-stated every 500 ms while easing with a 1,000 ms constant is a wall that always trails the circle the server burns against. SendPeriod writes the interval until the NEXT ce 01 of that state: SafeZoneUpdateIntervalMs while the ring is travelling, RingBlendMs otherwise. Fixed restores the flat RingBlendMs the tree shipped before D280.
